Why did Anita enter the forest reserve?
options: To capture photographs of rare birds
passage: Anita, a 29-year-old wildlife photographer, was trekking through a forest reserve early one morning. She often visited the area to capture pictures of rare birds. While walking along a narrow trail, she suddenly heard a soft whimpering sound. Curious and concerned, she followed the noise and discovered a young deer trapped in a thick bush. Its leg was caught in a tangled rope left behind by careless campers. The deer struggled in fear, and many people would have stayed away, afraid it might react unpredictably. But Anita knew she had to help. She spoke gently to calm the deer and slowly approached it. Using her pocketknife, she carefully cut the rope without hurting the animal. After a few tense minutes, the deer freed its leg and limped away into the forest. Anita felt relieved and proud. Saving the animal required calmness, patience, and courage. Later, she informed the forest department about the rope so they could prevent similar situations. That day, Anita realized that bravery often means stepping forward when others hesitate.
